title: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
description:

Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required

title: ALTCHA: Nil-map panic (pre-verification DoS) in v1 parseServerSignature on malformed VerificationData
description:
### Summary

`parseServerSignature` in the v1 module only initializes `ServerSignatureVerificationData.Extra` inside the `if err == nil` branch after `url.ParseQuery(parsedPayload.VerificationData)`. Go's `url.ParseQuery` returns the successfully-parsed pairs together with a non-nil error when the query string contains a malformed percent-escape. A subsequent loop unconditionally writes unknown keys into `Extra`, regardless of `err`, causing a nil-map write panic (assignment to entry in nil map)

title: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks
description:
A crafted PNG can make `imagemeta.Decode` allocate memory far in excess of the input file's size, leading to memory exhaustion. Two separate paths in the `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" branch are affected: the declared chunk length drives an allocation directly, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output bound. A 42-byte file allocated 256 MB, and a 127 KB file allocated 460 MB.

### Impact

Denial of service by memory exhaustion against any application that decodes untrusted

title: Bolt ListFormatHelper SQL injection
description:
### Impact

SQL Injection in ListFormatHelper allows authenticated users with the upload permission to execute arbitrary SQL queries and exfiltrate sensitive database contents through the /async/select-options endpoint when general/caching/list_format is enabled.

### Patches

This has been patched in Bolt 6.1.4.

title: Bolt: Prevent SSRF due to unchecked followed redirects
description:
### Impact

The `/bolt/async/upload-url` and `/bolt/async/embed` endpoints validated only the **submitted** URL before fetching it server-side, but the fetch then **followed redirects to destinations that were never re-validated**. This allowed an authenticated user to bypass the SSRF guard (`UrlSafetyChecker`) and make the server issue requests to internal/cloud-metadata addresses.

### Patches

This issue has been patched with Bolt 6.1.5.

title: Bolt: Information disclosure through unfiltered public relation API endpoint
description:
### Impact

A missing access-control filter in the public Relation API allowed unauthenticated users to discover metadata about unpublished, draft, and viewless content through REST and GraphQL endpoints.

### Patches

This has been patched in Bolt 6.1.4.

title: Bolt: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in URL-upload and embed endpoints
description:
### Impact

Two authenticated backend endpoints fetched a user-supplied URL server-side with no protection against internal targets.

### Patches

This has been patched in Bolt 6.1.4.

title: Bolt: Open redirect enables post-authentication redirection to arbitrary domains
description:
### Impact

Open redirect vulnerabilities in LoginFormAuthenticator allow attackers to redirect users to attacker-controlled domains after login success or login failure, enabling phishing attacks and potential token theft.

### Patches

This has been patched in Bolt 6.1.4.

title: Flyto2 Core: SSRF guard validates the resolved IP but connects by hostname, allowing DNS-rebinding TOCTOU
description:
## Summary
`validate_url_ssrf` resolves the hostname, checks the IP against private ranges, then **discards the IP and returns the hostname URL string**. aiohttp performs a fresh, independent DNS resolution at connect time. title: CVE-2026-126792 - A memory-safety flaw in the key-management request-building component of the library can lead to an
description: A memory-safety flaw in the key-management request-building component of the library can lead to an out-of-bounds write on the heap. A fixed-size output buffer is used under an assumption about cryptographic key size that is never validated, so when the library is embedded by a caller that supplies its own cryptographic callback implementation, data larger than the buffer can be written past its end. Exploitation requires the ability to control the embedding application's in-process key-management provider configuration, a high-privilege position. The demonstrated impact is memory corruption resulting in abnormal termination of the client process.

title: CVE-2026-126367 - @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. B
description: @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. Before 1.13.2, and from 1.14.0 through 1.14.1, the @grpc/grpc-js-xds SafeRegexValueMatcher and PathSafeRegexValueMatcher add start and end anchors without grouping a supplied top-level alternation. An expression intended to match one of several complete values can therefore match a prefix, substring, or suffix. The affected matchers are used for route selection, xDS credential identity matching, and RBAC URL path, principal name, server name, and header rules. An ALLOW policy using an alternation can consequently accept a method, certificate identity, or header value outside the intended set, while a DENY policy becomes broader rather than permissive. This issue is fixed in versions 1.13.2 and 1.14.2.

title: CVE-2026-126366 - MessagePack for Ruby is an implementation of the MessagePack binary serialization format. Prior to 1
description: MessagePack for Ruby is an implementation of the MessagePack binary serialization format. Prior to 1.8.7, the Java-platform msgpack gem for JRuby allocated arrays and byte buffers directly from attacker-controlled array32, str32, and bin32 declared sizes before confirming that corresponding elements or bytes were available. A short MessagePack header could therefore trigger a very large allocation or sustained heap growth when an application decoded untrusted input through MessagePack.unpack or MessagePack::Unpacker, potentially exhausting the shared JVM heap. map32 and declared counts at or above 2^31 did not use the affected allocation behavior. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.7.

title: CVE-2026-126365 - Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to @astrojs/prism 4.1.2, and from @astro
description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to @astrojs/prism 4.1.2, and from @astrojs/markdoc 0.3.0 until 2.1.2, runHighlighterWithAstro() returned code unchanged when Prism had no grammar for the requested language, and callers inserted that result as raw HTML. A code block labeled with an unsupported language could therefore render embedded HTML and script instead of displaying it as text. The Prism component was affected when applications supplied untrusted code with an unsupported or attacker-controlled lang, and the @astrojs/markdoc prism() extension was affected for less-trusted content authors even when Markdoc's ordinary HTML rendering was disabled. This issue is fixed in @astrojs/prism 4.1.2 and @astrojs/markdoc 2.1.2.

title: CVE-2026-126364 - Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpo
description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpoint compared the requested local-image path with the build output directory without preserving case on case-sensitive filesystems. A sibling directory whose path differed from the output directory only by letter case could therefore pass the containment check, allowing an unauthenticated requester to read image files accepted by the image service from outside the output directory. Exploitation required on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a preexisting case-variant sibling directory; ordinary traversal to unrelated paths was already rejected. This issue is fixed in Astro version 7.4.7.

title: CVE-2026-126363 - Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 0.2.0 until 7.1.2, the @astrojs/solid-js
description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 0.2.0 until 7.1.2, the @astrojs/solid-js renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. A request-controlled slot name containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Solid component using a client:* directive and dynamic access to the attacker-chosen slot property; a component that did not render that slot emitted only escaped fallback content. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2.

title: CVE-2026-126362 - Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte re
description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. Request-controlled slot names containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Svelte component using a client:* directive and dynamic rendering of the attacker-chosen slot; components that did not render that slot emitted only Astro's escaped fallback content. Both server rendering and client-side hydration used the unsafe slot name. This issue is fixed in version 9.1.2.

title: CVE-2026-126361 - Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to 7.4.5, Astro rendered a string used a
description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to 7.4.5, Astro rendered a string used as a dynamic element name as raw HTML after applying an incomplete character filter. A / in the string could make an HTML parser treat the remainder as attributes, allowing untrusted element-name input to inject event-handler markup. The .astro dynamic-tag renderer, JSX renderer, and MDX renderer were affected, and exploitation required an application to use request-controlled or stored untrusted data as all or part of an element name. This issue is fixed in version 7.4.5.

title: CVE-2026-126360 - OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.2, TraceContex
description: OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.2, TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-api can perform quadratic-time regular-expression backtracking on a malformed traceparent value containing a trace-context prefix, a long whitespace sequence, and an embedded newline. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled carrier that preserves embedded newlines and permits a sufficiently large value, because conforming HTTP header values cannot contain embedded newlines. JSON-based carriers, including applicable MCP request metadata integrations, can preserve the required newline depending on the SDK, instrumentation, and message-size limits. Parsing on an asynchronous server's event-loop thread can consume excessive CPU and delay unrelated requests, while the advisory does not establish disclosure, modification, or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.45.2.

title: CVE-2026-126359 - Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 3.12.0 un
description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 3.12.0 until 4.13.16, the css helper in hono/css escapes interpolated string values separately and therefore fails to neutralize a closing style tag when < ends the template text or a preceding value and / begins the next attacker-controlled value. During server-side rendering, the combined output can close the <Style /> element early and cause the remainder of the interpolated value to be interpreted as HTML. Applications that place an untrusted string immediately after < in a css template, including adjacent untrusted interpolations, can expose viewers to attacker-controlled HTML or script and information accessible to that page. Other uses of the css helper are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

title: CVE-2026-126358 - Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.1.4 unt
description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.1.4 until 4.13.16, RegExpRouter can omit wildcard middleware in three version-specific cases: since 4.13.0, middleware using the explicit default parameter pattern in /api/:tenant{[^/]+}/admin/* is not applied to a route written as /api/:tenant/admin/:id; since 4.1.4, middleware on /admin/* is not applied to a route registered as /admin* for paths under /admin/; and since 4.4.0, a request path containing an encoded line terminator can reach the not-found handler without wildcard middleware. The default SmartRouter selects RegExpRouter for most applications, and the router's registration-time coverage calculation treated the first two matching pattern pairs as different while its compiled wildcard did not match line terminators in the third case. An unauthenticated client can reach a route handler or the not-found handler without authentication or authorization middleware registered on the wildcard path. TrieRouter, LinearRouter, and PatternRouter apply the middleware in the three described cases. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

title: CVE-2026-126357 - Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.
description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.16, mount() and app.mount() can remove a dynamic mount prefix using the route-pattern length rather than the matched-prefix length, allowing a crafted path to be forwarded as a protected inner route while the outer application routes the original path. Since 4.12.21, rebuilding the forwarded URL from the decoded pathname can also convert a decoded backslash to a slash and collapse parent-directory segments, again causing the mounted application to receive a protected path. An unauthenticated client can use either applicable path transformation to reach a mounted route without authentication or authorization middleware scoped to a subpath inside the mount prefix. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

title: CVE-2026-126356 - Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.5.1 unt
description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.5.1 until 4.13.16, validator('form') uses a strict whole-header pattern that fails to recognize multipart/form-data when its Content-Type includes another legal parameter or extra whitespace after a semicolon. The validation callback receives an empty object even though c.req.parseBody() or c.req.formData() can still parse and expose all submitted fields to the handler. An unauthenticated client can therefore bypass allow-list or required-field checks when the application relies on the form validator and its callback accepts an empty object. application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

title: CVE-2026-126355 - Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.
description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.16, csrf() limits origin validation to the content types normally sent by HTML forms and therefore does not validate text/ping requests generated by Chromium hyperlink auditing. Chrome and Edge can send a cross-origin credentialed POST without a CORS preflight through an <a ping> action, and the middleware then skips both Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks. The fixed request body limits exploitation to state-changing endpoints whose effect is selected by the path or query string and does not depend on submitted body data. The user's cookie must accompany the request, which generally requires a same-site origin or a cookie configured with SameSite=None, and Firefox does not send hyperlink-auditing pings by default. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.
